info.title: OpenAPI For Cargo Insurance
info.description: APIs to run a marine open cover for your customers: apply for the policy, issue it, and declare shipments under it

get.description: Every list of values the cargo endpoints accept: customer roles, transport modes, goods categories, packaging, conditions, characteristics, Incoterms, currencies and countries. Each entry has the `value` to send and a `label` to show. Build your dropdowns from this response instead of hard-coding them, so a new value reaches your users without a release on your side.

200.description: The options, one list per key

post.description:
Registers the business the cargo is insured for, by its commercial registration (CR) number. When the commercial registry knows the business, its legal name and address come from there and the customer is `verified`; anything you send for those fields is ignored. When it does not, the call answers `40031`: send it again with `legal_name` and `address`, and the customer is kept as entered, `unverified`.

Registering a CR number you already registered updates that customer and answers `200` instead of `201`.

role.description: The business's part in the trade. One of the `customer_roles` values from Get the options.

contact.description: The person at the business to contact about its policies.

legal_name.description: Only used when the registry has no record of the CR number.

country.description: Two-letter country code, one of the `countries` values.

address.description: Only used when the registry has no record of the CR number. `street` and `city` are required when it is sent.

200.description: The customer you had already registered, updated

400.description: `40031` when the commercial registry has no record of the CR number and `legal_name` or `address` is missing.

post.description:
Applies for a marine open cover: a one-year policy that the business declares its shipments under. The application answers the insurance company's proposal questions: what the business does, what it ships, from where to where and how, how much it expects to ship in the year, the most any one shipment will be worth, and its claims of the last five years.

The answer is always `201`; read its `status`. `approved`: `quote` holds the terms and a policy can be issued. `referred`: an underwriter is reviewing it; read the application again until the status changes. `rejected`: it cannot be insured, and `reasons` says why.

When it is `approved`, `quote` holds the rate every declared shipment is charged at (`declaration_rate_percent`) and the deposit paid up front to start the policy (`total_price`, VAT included).

currency.description: The currency of every amount in the application. One of the `currencies` values from Get the options.

post.description:
Accepts the quote of an approved open-cover application. The policy comes back unpaid (`status` `0`, `coverage_confirmed` `false`) with a `payment_link`. Send the customer to that page to pay the deposit. Once the payment succeeds the policy is issued: it gets its policy number, schedule and tax invoice, its year of cover starts that day, and the customer is sent on to your `redirect_url`.

Calling this again for the same application before it is paid returns the same policy, updated.

redirect_url.description: Where to send the customer after they pay. `policyID` anywhere in it is replaced with the policy's id.

post.description:
Declares one shipment under an open-cover policy. A shipment inside the policy's terms (its countries of origin and destination, its transport modes and its limit per shipment) is covered at once: `status` is `issued` and `certificate_url` is its certificate. A shipment outside them is `referred` to an underwriter, and `reasons` says why; read the declaration again until it is `issued` or `rejected`.

`premium` is what the shipment costs at the policy's rate. Declared premiums are reported here and totalled on the policy; they are not paid through a payment link.

`shipment.departure_date` has to fall within the policy period.

400.description: `40027` when the open-cover policy is not paid for and issued yet, or is past its last day.

example.message: Shipments can be declared once the open-cover policy is paid for and issued, and until its last day.

valuation_basis.description: What a declared shipment is insured for when it names no amount. `cif_plus_10`: the invoice value plus freight and other costs, plus 10%.

declaration_rate_percent.description: The rate every declared shipment is charged at, as a percentage of its insured amount.

valid_until.description: The last day the quote can be accepted.
